stops.note: named the wooden frame used to smoke and preserve meat
French settlers in the Caribbean adopted the word for the same smoking technique
stops.meaning: a wooden frame for smoking meat

stops.note: applied to hunters who smoked meat this way, many of whom turned to piracy
anglicized from French to describe Caribbean pirates
stops.meaning: a pirate, especially one who raided Spanish ships in the Caribbean

current_meaning: a pirate or lawless adventurer, especially historically in the Caribbean
